# MT7628KN Wi-Fi Extender

> 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi extender (MediaTek MT7628KN, eCos firmware) with an HTTP configuration page, a small HTTP API and a Telnet console.

Use this device's current HTTP origin; no fixed IP is required. Credentials, when set, come from the owner. This file and /agent_api.txt contain no credentials and are readable without signing in.

Ask the owner before changing connectivity, credentials, restarting or writing firmware. Never infer authorization from this file.

## Factory defaults

- Device network: open (no password), named "Extender-" followed by the Wi-Fi MAC in uppercase without colons, for example Extender-A03E9C1D0E54.
- Mode: access point (Ethernet uplink), bridged; the device takes its own address from the upstream router by DHCP and runs no DHCP server. Clients on its network get addresses from the upstream router.
- Admin: user "admin", no password; the page opens without signing in. Telnet is disabled.
- Rescue address 192.168.11.1 is always present on the LAN side in addition to the DHCP address.
- Holding the reset button for more than 4 seconds restores these defaults and restarts (about one minute). A short press only restarts.

## Find the device

1. Join the "Extender-..." network (factory defaults) or the configured device network, or use the same LAN as its Ethernet cable.
2. The device address is the DHCP lease for its MAC on the upstream router. Without router access: from a client on the device network, use the router's address space (the device bridges), or set a static address in 192.168.11.0/24 on a wired client and use http://192.168.11.1/.
3. Confirm with GET /wifi_state.html: JSON with "chip":"MT7628KN".

## Set up from factory defaults

Do these in order. After each POST, check the response is OK; for Wi-Fi changes poll GET /wifi_state.html every 2 seconds until busy=0, revision increased, error=0 and saved=1.

1. Inspect: GET /wifi_state.html. Note mode, ssid, device_security, admin_password_set.
2. Secure administration first: POST /admin_apply.html USER=admin&PASSWORD=<new>&CONFIRM=<new>&CURRENT= . Then use HTTP Basic authentication with these credentials on every later request (except /llms.txt and /agent_api.txt).
3. Choose the uplink:
   - Ethernet (access point): keep the cable to the router; MODE=ap and a CHANNEL of your choice (1, 6 or 11 are usual).
   - Wi-Fi (repeater): unplug the Ethernet cable first (a cable to the same network plus a wireless uplink makes a bridge loop). GET /wifi_scan.html, pick the network, and use its channel and security (WPA2PSK/AES = wpa2, WPA1PSKWPA2PSK/... = mixed, NONE = open; WPA3/SAE and enterprise are unsupported).
4. Secure the device network and apply, in one request:
   - Access point: POST /wifi_apply.html MODE=ap&SSID=<name>&DEVICE_SECURITY=wpa2&PASSWORD=<8-63 chars>&CHANNEL=<1-13>
   - Repeater: POST /wifi_apply.html MODE=repeater&SSID=<name>&DEVICE_SECURITY=wpa2&PASSWORD=<8-63 chars>&CHANNEL=<uplink channel>&UPLINK_SSID=<network>&UPLINK_SECURITY=<wpa2|mixed|open>&UPLINK_PASSWORD=<password>
   Wi-Fi restarts; if you are connected over Wi-Fi, reconnect to the new SSID with the new password. The DHCP address may change.
5. Verify: GET /wifi_state.html shows the new mode and ssid, device_security=wpa2, admin_password_set=1 and telnet=1. In repeater mode uplink_status must be "connected"; "disconnected" usually means a wrong uplink password or channel, and the device network stays up so you can correct it. Finally test traffic (for example a web request) from a client on the device network.

Telnet (TCP 23, same admin credentials) becomes available only after steps 2 and 4. It is for diagnostics and firmware installation; see /agent_api.txt.

## Optional: remote access (ntun)

The device can keep an encrypted reverse tunnel (ntun, Noise IK; https://github.com/eloirotava/ntun) to an ntun server, so its web page or Telnet is reachable from 127.0.0.1 on that server. Off by default; needs an admin password.

1. GET /wifi_state.html and read ntun.public_key (the device generates its key at first boot; it survives factory resets and the private half never leaves the device).
2. Register that public key on the ntun server (server-side step, done by the owner).
3. POST /ntun_apply.html ENABLED=1&HOST=<server>&PORT=<port, ntun default 8222>&SERVER_KEY=<server public key, 64 hex>&LOCAL_PORT=<80 for the web page or 23 for Telnet>. The device saves and restarts.
4. After about one minute, GET /wifi_state.html: ntun.state "connected" means the tunnel is up; ntun.status explains errors (for example an unregistered device key).

## Recovery

- Lost credentials or a broken configuration: hold the reset button for more than 4 seconds, then start again from factory defaults.
- Device unreachable after a Wi-Fi change: reconnect to the configured device network; if it is gone, connect by Ethernet and use the DHCP address or http://192.168.11.1/.
- A power cycle always boots the installed firmware.

## Reference

- [Configuration page](/): the same operations for people.
- [Agent API reference](/agent_api.txt): all fields, validation rules, state fields, scan format and firmware procedures.
- [Current state](/wifi_state.html): JSON; passwords are never returned.
